vares-adriatic-metals.conditions_add: EBRD's own project summary document for this investment says a condition of the equity financing requires the company to bring all of its activities into line with the bank's environmental and social requirements, including preparing and disclosing an impact assessment for the Vares mine. The same document says an Environmental and Social Action Plan had to be agreed between the EBRD and the company before the share subscription was signed. EBRD's complaints office repeated both points in 2023.

why.safeguard: a condition of the equity financing requires the company to bring all of its activities into line with the bank's environmental and social requirements

vares-adriatic-metals.searched: Opened the EBRD project summary document for project 52342 in full (fetched with curl after WebFetch was blocked by an unanswered permission prompt, not by the host). It contains the words condition and required three times about this deal: 'A condition of equity financing requires the Company to align all of its activities with EBRD's E&S requirements'; 'The Environmental and Social Action Plan will be agreed between the EBRD and the client prior to the signing of the Subscription Agreement'; and, in the October 2021 update, 'As a condition of EBRD's equity subscription, Adriatic Metals is required to prepare and disclose an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) in line with EBRD's Performance Requirements for the Vares mining project.' Also read the IPAM assessment report of March 2023, which states the same condition and says the agreed action plan specified that the company was required to develop and disclose the impact assessment. Also read the Early Warning System mirror page for EBRD-52342, which lists no terms. Probed for a published copy of the action plan itself at the EBRD document paths used for other projects' action plans; all returned 404, so the plan's text is not public. This is not just shareholder monitoring: the equity subscription itself carried the term.

shah-deniz-sangachal.conditions_add: EBRD lent to a company holding 10 per cent of the field, not to the project, and its own project summary document says the normal bank-client relationship that would let it set contractual requirements for operations at the site does not exist here. The loan did carry environmental, health and safety monitoring and reporting requirements, which the lenders met by paying an independent consultant to review the project each year. EBRD's board agreed that no Environmental and Social Action Plan was required, because the borrower could not make the operator, BP, do anything.
shah-deniz-sangachal.ct_note: We looked for a term EBRD attached to its money for the Shah Deniz 2 expansion and the Sangachal Terminal. EBRD's own project document says it set no requirements for operations at the site, because its borrower was a 10 per cent shareholder and not the operator. The only term on the loan was annual monitoring and reporting by an outside consultant.

why.safeguard: The loan did carry environmental, health and safety monitoring and reporting requirements, which the lenders met by paying an independent consultant to review the project each year.

shah-deniz-sangachal.searched: Opened the EBRD project summary documents for all three Lukoil Shah Deniz loans in full: 46766 (the 2015 A/B loan, EBRD arranging USD 500 million), 49215 (a further USD 100 million in 2017, later cancelled) and 45599 (a USD 200 million loan in 2014 for the Stage 1 extension). The 46766 document says plainly: 'A unique aspect of this transaction is that EBRD has no formal relationship (for this project) with the technical operator, BP... Therefore, the normal Bank-Client relationship, allowing EBRD to influence or to make contractual requirements for operations at the site, does not exist on this project.' The 49215 document says 'All EHS monitoring and reporting requirements on the loan to date have been satisfied', which is the one term on the money. Read the full EBRD compliance review report of the 2017 complaint (both halves, about 152,000 characters), which states: 'As LOSD does not have the ability to influence implementation of additional measures by the Operator, the Board of EBRD agreed no ESAP is required.' The words condition, covenant, loan agreement and disbursement do not appear anywhere in that report. Also read the independent consultant's 2017 monitoring report, which says the lenders require independent health, safety, environment and community monitoring, and the operator's own management summary, which is a BP document and carries no lender term. Also checked the Early Warning System mirrors for 46766 and 49215 and the EBRD and Accountability Console complaint records; none carries a financing term. Looked for a direct EBRD project for Shah Deniz 2 or the Sangachal Terminal and found none in this period: EBRD's only money in the expansion went through the 10 per cent shareholder. An action plan does exist for the earlier Shah Deniz Stage 1 and pipeline appraisal, but that is a different phase and is not recorded here.

ipp4-al-manakher-easep-detention.conditions_add: EBRD's compliance review report says the client was required to deliver an annual environmental and social report covering stakeholder engagement and grievances from June 2016, and that the project's mitigation and monitoring plan stood in for the action plan the bank's policy required. OPIC's public project summary says the plant was required to meet two sets of IFC pollution guidelines, to commission an independent third-party audit showing compliance with its environmental and social covenants, and to produce a noise mitigation plan and a health and safety plan. As part of processing the loan EBRD approved a derogation from its own limit on nitrogen oxide emissions.

why.safeguard: required to meet two sets of IFC pollution guidelines, to commission an independent third-party audit showing compliance with its environmental and social covenants
why.admin: required to deliver an annual environmental and social report covering stakeholder engagement and grievances from June 2016

ipp4-al-manakher-easep-detention.searched: Opened the EBRD project summary document for project 44284 in full. It describes a secured limited recourse loan of up to USD 100 million and says a derogation from the bank's own 2008 environmental and social policy was required because the plant would not meet EU limits for nitrogen oxide emissions. It lists no action plan and no condition of disbursement. Read the non-technical summary and the mitigation and monitoring programme published on EBRD's site; the programme is a consultant's document for the company, and the words action plan, covenant, loan agreement and disbursement do not appear in it. Found the EBRD complaints registry entry for complaint 2015/02, pulled out the document links, and read the compliance review report of December 2016, which supplies the two EBRD terms quoted above and records quarterly audits of operations by the lenders' own engineer. OPIC's record had never been opened before: its two public project summaries are still on the DFC website and the final one sets out the clearest requirements on this case, including the phrase 'environmental and social covenants'. The 2015 and 2016 annual reports of EBRD's complaints office carry no terms, only the case's progress. Nothing in any of these documents attaches a condition to the detention of the complainant; the review found the bank compliant.
